proposed_from.topic: Finite-sample conditional certification and a same-class minimax lower benchmark for one-network graphon indirect derivatives. In the Li--Wager finite-rank sparse-graphon subclass with Bernoulli(1/2) assignment, anonymous treated-neighbor-fraction interference, known response and C3 radii B and L, and C_log log n <= d=o(n), target the realized finite-population midpoint indirect derivative. Construct the exact degree-adaptive discrete score, a polynomial-time first-Hoeffding-projection PC-balanced estimator, and a graph-observable finite-sample conditional confidence interval with explicit bias and bounded-difference variance certificates retaining isolates. Prove exact score moments and first two Hoeffding projections, the graph-conditional isolate wall, and same-class linear, local C3-bump, and degree-lattice lower bounds whose supported analytic envelope has graph-floor, interior, and lattice phases for minimax absolute risk and interval expected length. Establish a lower-upper bracket using the conservative feasible envelope; do not claim that the feasible envelope matches the lower benchmark, a sharp minimax or honest expected-length rate, or an achieved frontier. Leave a rate-sharp feasible PC construction at logarithmic degree open.
proposed_from.novelty_justification: {"published_axis":"LiWager2022RandomGraph is the closest theorem-level comparator. Its Theorem 6 proves a pointwise Gaussian limit at rate \\(\\sqrt{\\rho_n}=\\sqrt{d/n}\\) for a global PC-balancing estimator and its Discussion says that the optimal indirect-effect rate remains open. The selected kernel keeps the same Bernoulli probability, anonymous-interference target, and finite-rank sparse-graphon structure, but changes the statistical experiment at the first nontrivial proof step: the score is localized to a shrinking binomial window and then spectrally residualized. The desired result derives a constrained envelope with a lattice regime, an interior nonparametric regime, and the published graph floor; proves a feasible-PC upper bound uniform over every admissible bandwidth; and matches both absolute risk and honest expected length with four same-class lower-bound submodels. ArmstrongKolesar2020SimpleHonest supplies the deterministic-bias confidence geometry but has independent fixed-design regression observations and no graph projector, exposure lattice, or graph floor. CaiLow2004Adaptation supplies expected-length lower-bound inequalities but not the network experiment modulus. HuLiWager2022AverageDirectIndirect identifies the policy meaning of the target but gives no estimator or frontier. seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Li--Wager's global treatment score is replaced by a bandwidth-indexed discrete derivative score whose squared norm grows as \(h^{-3}\); the empirical-projector expansion must therefore be uniform in \(h\) and retain the exact local moment cancellations.
seed_details.referee_objection: Immediate from LiWager2022RandomGraph and ArmstrongKolesar2020SimpleHonest because one only localizes their score and adds a bias bound.
seed_details.rebuttal: Neither paper controls estimated-PC residualization for an exploding localized score, the binomial lattice endpoints, or a same-class lower bound for honest expected length; Li and Wager explicitly leave the optimal indirect-effect rate open.

proposed_from.literature_map: Li and Wager (2022, Annals of Statistics, Theorem 6 and Section 4.3) provide the direct anchor: in a finite-rank sparse graphon they use estimated principal-component balancing to obtain a Gaussian limit for the same population average indirect derivative, and their Discussion explicitly leaves its optimal rate open. Their proof first balances the graphon eigenfunctions, then expands the feasible score through an empirical-projector lemma, isolates an asymmetric bilinear leading term, and applies a local-dependence Gaussian approximation. Armstrong and Kolesar (2020, Quantitative Economics, Sections 2--3 and supplemental finite-sample bias theorem) provide the honest-inference method: compute a worst-case smoothness bias, combine it with the stochastic radius, and choose bandwidth for confidence length rather than undersmoothing. Cai and Low (2004, Annals of Statistics, Theorems 1--3) provide the testing-to-expected-length bridge through between-class and ordered moduli. Hu, Li, and Wager (2022, Biometrika, Theorem 1) establish that the average direct and indirect effects sum to the derivative of the Bernoulli policy value, fixing the causal interpretation at assignment probability one half. Abbe, Fan, Wang, and Zhong (2020, Annals of Statistics, Theorem 2.1) give entrywise eigenvector linearization for low-expected-rank matrices, while Tang and Cape (2025, arXiv, Theorems 1--3 and the rank-adaptive test) show how growing-rank two-to-infinity expansions and thresholding work for graph inference. Leung (2022, Econometrica) treats approximate-neighborhood dependence and inference for level effects rather than a graphon-localized derivative. Bhadra and Schweinberger (2025, arXiv survey, Sections 4--6) distinguish fixed-network and random-network inference and list external validity as unresolved; their separate 2025 preprint studies linear conditional-mean spillovers and does not contain a smooth derivative or honest-length frontier. Searches through September 2026 found no theorem combining the Li--Wager target and class, a discrete local derivative score, a bandwidth constrained by the binomial exposure lattice, a feasible spectral-residualization bound uniform down to logarithmic degree, and matched absolute-risk and honest expected-length lower bounds.
